nodes.summary: The claim of Scottish Book Problem 176 is false: there are a complete normed ring $A$ that is a normed algebra over $\mathbb{R}$ and elements $a, b \in A$ with $ab = 1$ and $ba = 1$ such that $b$ is not the limit of any sequence $(p_n(a))_{n \ge 0}$ with $p_n$ real polynomials.
nodes.title: Eidelheit's Problem 176 has a negative answer

nodes.summary: The claim that in every complete normed ring $A$ (so $\|xy\| \le \|x\| \, \|y\|$, and $A$ has a unit) that is a normed algebra over $\mathbb{R}$, the inverse of every invertible element is a limit of real polynomials in that element: whenever $a, b \in A$ satisfy $ab = 1$ and $ba = 1$, there is a sequence $(p_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of real polynomials with $p_n(a) \to b$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Scottish Book Problem 176 (Eidelheit's claim)
